blocks.content: A seismograph is the instrument that records ground motion, whereas the seismogram is the resulting graph depicting wave arrivals and amplitude.

rows: An instrument or apparatus that detects and measures seismic waves.
The physical or digital record generated by a seismograph.
Senses ground displacement during seismic events.
Displays wave amplitudes, frequencies, and arrival times.

items: S-waves cannot pass through liquids, proving the Earth's outer core is liquid—frequently tested in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Richter Scale is logarithmic and measures magnitude (energy released), while the Mercalli Scale measures intensity (visible damage from I to XII).
The focus (hypocenter) is the origin point inside Earth, while the epicenter lies directly above it on the surface.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A seismograph is the physical instrument used to detect and record earthquake waves.
A seismogram is the graphic record or visual output produced by a seismograph.
Seismograms record three main wave types in order: Primary (P) waves, Secondary (S) waves, and Surface waves.
The time interval between the arrival of P-waves and S-waves on a seismogram determines the distance to the epicenter.
